_what_this_is: ONE place naming the concepts this repo stores on disk, and every SPELLING each concept actually has. Written 20 September 2026 after a question about the repo was answered twice in one day by grepping for ONE literal string and reporting the empty result as the answer to a broader question. 'Does this file contain the string extracted_at' is not 'does this record carry an observation date': memory/browse_sources/*.json carry data_date. When a concept has two names on disk, a grep for one spelling is wrong by construction, and it is wrong in the most expensive direction - it returns nothing, and nothing reads like an answer.
_the_rule: A question of the form 'does X carry a <concept>' is answered from this file, through tools/ask.py, and never from an ad-hoc grep. tools/ask.py reads this file at runtime; it holds no spelling of its own, so adding a spelling here is the whole change.
_how_to_add_a_spelling: Do NOT invent one. Find it on disk or in code, and record where. Every entry below carries found_in (a real path in this repo when the census found one) and written_by (the code that produces it), and both were read on the date in _censused. A spelling nobody could point at is a guess, and a guess in this file is worse than a missing entry: the tool would report a concept present where the disk says nothing.
_censused: 20 September 2026. memory/**/*.json: 5145 files parsed, every dict key matching /(date|_at$|_ts$|^ts$|time|stamp|observed|fetched|as_of|asof)/i counted. core/*.py: every string literal matching /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/ against the same pattern, via AST. core/provenance.py:121 OBSERVED_FIELD contributed the six per-source year fields, which is itself a second registry of this same concept and is the clearest evidence that one was needed.

_shapes.iso_datetime: full ISO 8601; a naive value is read as UTC
_shapes.year: a bare year, 2025 or '2025' - aged from 31 December of that year, because a year-resolution observation is not more precise than the year
_shapes.year_fraction: YYYY.f, e.g. 2026.101 - a decimal fraction of the year
_shapes.year_map: an object of {name: year}; the OLDEST value is the record's observation date, because a composite is as old as its oldest number

OBSERVATION_DATE.means: WHEN THE THING WAS OBSERVED, or the date the observed value refers to. Not when the file was written, not when the record was processed, not when a row was cached for convenience. This is the concept core.measurement_honesty.observation_age_days ages, and the one core/notary.py's age dimension asks every step for.

not_this.revision_date: core/provenance.py:220 writes it and its own comment says so in as many words: a number for 2023 can be reworked in 2026, so a revision is a DIFFERENT fact from an observation. Present in memory/provenance_latest.json (22 occurrences, all None today).
not_this.timestamp / ts / cycle_ts / mtime / comp: processing times - when this program did something. memory/axis_history.json carries BOTH per entry: 'date' is the observation and 'timestamp' is when the row was written. Using one for the other is the defect this file exists to prevent.
not_this.observed_date: ZERO occurrences in the census. Listed here so the next reader knows it was looked for and is not a spelling this repo uses.
not_this.observation_date: ZERO occurrences in the census. Same.

spellings.means: the date the value refers to
the instant the value was extracted from a live page - for a live fetch this IS the observation
spellings.note: One occurrence on disk, and a whole night's provenance decision rests on it: config/step_inputs.json declares it as browser_scout's live_fetch timestamp_field.

spellings.means: the canonical name in the honesty layer - core.measurement_honesty.observation_age_days takes exactly this
when the section was fetched from its source
when a transcript was fetched and cached; for these records the fetch is the observation
observation date of the CO2 reading
observation year of the temperature anomaly
observation point of the sea-level reading
observation year of the displacement figure
observation year of the conflict count
observation year of the nuclear-stockpile figure
per-indicator observation years for a World Bank section; the section is as old as its oldest number
the observation date of an axis-history row
spellings.caveat: AMBIGUOUS AND DELIBERATELY REGISTERED ANYWAY. 'date' is the observation date in memory/axis_history.json, where each row carries 'date' for the observation and 'timestamp' for when the row was written - but the same four letters are used elsewhere for things that are not observations. tools/ask.py prints this caveat next to any match on this spelling, so a hit on 'date' is reported as a lead and never as a settled answer.

OBSERVATION_RECORD.means: The shape of ONE observation at ingest: a panel yields N of these, one per (entity, period), or none. Added 21 Sep 2026 after a World Bank panel of 17,490 cells was collapsed into a single card carrying value 83.3899993896484, unit 'unknown', no country and no year. Measured against the real body, that number is AFE / 2024.
OBSERVATION_RECORD._the_rule: NO PLACEHOLDER IN A REQUIRED FIELD. unit:'unknown', entity:'unknown', period:null are forbidden: a placeholder passes every check that only tests presence, which makes it worse than absence. A record missing a required field is emitted UNVERIFIED with a reason naming the field.
OBSERVATION_RECORD._three_timestamps: period is a property of the DATUM, published_at of the SOURCE, retrieved_at of US. None substitutes for another: today we can read a value that refers to 1990, and the fetch date says nothing about it.
OBSERVATION_RECORD._one_door: core/observation_record.py::extract is the only code that builds one.

spellings.means: ISO3 country code, or an aggregate code the SOURCE ITSELF declares as one. Never inferred from the shape of the code.
the period the VALUE refers to. Not when it was fetched.
year | month | day | instant — how precise `period` is.
the number itself.
the unit AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Never 'unknown'; a missing unit makes the record UNVERIFIED.
the VERBATIM slice of the fetched body carrying the value, entity and period. Never rebuilt from the parsed object.
the address fetched.
the path that selected THIS row.
the SOURCE's own publication/update stamp, if it gives one; else absent.
the moment WE fetched. Never a substitute for period.
